primaryEvidence.finding: The regional urban-network chapter explicitly names El Faouar among the settlements that expanded toward the Saharan/frontier zone. Its definition of agglomeration includes cities, villages and small towns regardless of communal status. This supports inhabited-settlement identity, not equivalence with any sector, municipality or delegation territory.

sourceIdentityQualifications.identity: The stable inhabited-place source node and official urban-settlement description support a single picker display association with El Faouar base485. Retain village kind, coordinates, raw names/aliases/context, prayer reference485, five sectors and all existing Ghidma/manual-point and Rejim Maatoug transfer decisions. This is no polygon or city-sector identity claim.
limits: Ghidma has a pre-existing source polygon/delegation disagreement, explicitly documented by its active administrative_context curation. Preserve that reviewed metadata and the unmodified source polygon; it does not justify changing the proposed Faouar city association.
Two historical Faouar-coded sectors are current Rejim Maatoug sectors. Their existing transfer decisions and complete groups remain unchanged.
No exact GPS coordinate, inhabited perimeter or municipal boundary is certified by this display review.
Phone evidence is handled separately by root; this report does not claim to have viewed the phone.
